notes.statement: Alhopuro et al. (2008) noted that the zebrafish meltdown (mlt) phenotype, caused by a recessive ATPase-activating germline mutation in smooth-muscle myosin (smmhc/myh11), develops intestinal abnormalities reminiscent of human Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and juvenile polyposis.

The mlt zebrafish develops intestinal abnormalities reminiscent of human Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS) and juvenile polyposis (JP).

notes.statement: Alhopuro et al. (2008) screened MYH11 in patients with colorectal cancer, PJS, and juvenile polyposis. They found somatic protein-elongating frameshift mutations in 55% of colorectal cancers with microsatellite instability and a germline frameshift in 1 individual with PJS. They also found two somatic missense mutations, R501L and K1044N, in one microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer.
quotes: we searched for MYH11 mutations in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), PJS and JP.
We found somatic protein-elongating frameshift mutations in 55% of CRCs displaying microsatellite instability and in the germ-line of one individual with PJS.
Additionally, two somatic missense mutations were found in one microsatellite stable CRC.

notes.statement: Alhopuro et al. (2008) found that the MYH11 frameshift mutations and the missense mutations R501L and K1044N all produced unregulated molecules with constitutive motor activity, similar to the mutant myosin underlying the zebrafish mlt phenotype. The authors suggested that MYH11 mutations appear to contribute to human intestinal neoplasia.
quotes: All mutations resulted in unregulated molecules displaying constitutive motor activity, similar to the mutant myosin underlying mlt.
Thus, MYH11 mutations appear to contribute also to human intestinal neoplasia.

quotes: Generalized intestinal polyposis and melanin spots of the oral mucosa, lips and digits; a syndrome of diagnostic significance.

quotes: investigated the loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at the LKB1 locus by real-time fluorescence polymerase chain reaction genotyping using a fluorescent resonance energy transfer technique. The results suggest a different mechanism from LOH in the formation of hamartomatous polyps.

notes.statement: Amos et al. (2004) found that individuals with PJS carrying missense mutations of STK11 had a significantly later time to onset of first polypectomy (p = 0.04) and of other symptoms compared with those with truncating mutations or no detectable mutation.
quotes: Individuals with missense mutations had a significantly later time to onset of first polypectomy (p = 0.04) and of other symptoms compared with those participants either with truncating mutations or no detectable mutation.

notes.statement: In a historical cohort of 51 individuals with PJS who completed questionnaires, Amos et al. (2004) found a median time to onset of gastrointestinal symptoms or polypectomy of 13 years, with wide variability; gastric polyps were frequent, with a median age at onset of 16 years.
quotes: used a historical cohort design to study 51 individuals with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome who had completed self-administered questionnaires
The median time to onset for gastrointestinal symptoms or polypectomy was 13 years of age but showed a wide variability.

notes.statement: Amos et al. (2004) detected STK11 mutations in 22 of 32 (69%) PJS probands but in none of 10 probands referred to rule out PJS, and real-time PCR found no large deletions in mutation-negative patients; they concluded that STK11 testing should be restricted to individuals meeting PJS criteria or their close relatives.
quotes: Real-time PCR analysis to quantitate DNA failed to detect any large deletions in PJS participants without STK11 mutations.

notes.statement: Le Meur et al. (2004) used quantitative multiplex PCR of short fluorescent fragments (QMPSF) of the 19p13 region and found an approximately 250-kb heterozygous deletion removing the entire STK11 gene in a family with PJS. This was the first reported complete germline deletion of STK11. The authors suggested that large genomic deletions should be considered in PJS families without detectable STK11 point mutations.
quotes: This report, which constitutes the first description of a complete germline deletion of STK11, shows that the presence of such large genomic deletions should be considered in PJS families without detectable point mutations of STK11.

notes.statement: Le Meur et al. (2004) noted that STK11 germline mutations are detected in only 50 to 70% of PJS families, which had suggested genetic heterogeneity of the disease.
quotes: The detection of STK11 germline mutations, in only 50-70% of PJS families, has suggested a genetic heterogeneity of the disease.

notes.statement: Keller et al. (2001) reviewed the history of the combination of intestinal polyposis with pigmentation of the skin and mucous membranes. Their review covered the work of Jan Peutz and Harold Jeghers, after whom the syndrome is named.
quotes: Jan Peutz, Harold Jeghers and a remarkable combination of polyposis and pigmentation of the skin and mucous membranes.

notes.statement: WILLIAMS and KNUDSEN (1965) reported Peutz-Jeghers syndrome with metastasizing duodenal carcinoma.
quotes: PEUTZ-JEGHERS SYNDROME WITH METASTASIZING DUODENAL CARCINOMA.

notes.statement: CHRISTIAN et al. (1964) reported Peutz-Jeghers syndrome associated with a functioning ovarian tumor.
quotes: PEUTZ-JEGHERS SYNDROME ASSOCIATED WITH FUNCTIONING OVARIAN TUMOR.

notes.statement: SHEWARD (1962) reported Peutz-Jeghers syndrome in childhood with unusual radiological features.
quotes: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome in childhood: unusual radiological fetures.

notes.statement: BARTHOLOMEW et al. (1962) reported on intestinal polyposis associated with mucocutaneous pigmentation.
quotes: Intestinal polyposis associated with mucocutaneous pigmentation.

notes.statement: DORMANDY (1957) described Peutz-Jeghers syndrome as gastrointestinal polyposis with mucocutaneous pigmentation.
quotes: Gastrointestinal polyposis with mucocutaneous pigmentation (Peutz-Jeghers syndrome).

notes.statement: BRUWER et al. (1954) used the name Peutz-Jeghers syndrome for the combination of surface pigmentation and generalized intestinal polyposis.
quotes: Surface pigmentation and generalized intestinal polyposis; (Peutz-Jeghers syndrome).

notes.statement: Buchet-Poyau et al. (2002) noted that STK11 mutations could not be detected in a considerable number of PJS patients, suggesting genetic heterogeneity, and studied family PJS07, which lacked STK11 mutations and showed linkage to 19q13.3-q13.4 between markers D19S180 and D19S254.
quotes: However, in a considerable number of PJS-patients mutations cannot be detected in STK11 suggesting genetic heterogeneity.
In this study we investigated candidate genes within markers D19S180 and D19S254, since multipoint linkage analysis yielded significant LOD scores for this region in this family.

notes.statement: Buchet-Poyau et al. (2002) found no pathogenic mutations in all exons and exon-intron junctions of PSCD2, KLK10, PRKCG, and STK13 in affected members of family PJS07, providing considerable evidence for exclusion of these genes as the second PJS locus on 19q13.3-q13.4. They also excluded STK11IP (LIP1) on 2q36 in this family, although it could be a candidate in other non-STK11 families.
quotes: No pathogenic mutation was identified in these four genes in affected individuals.
These data provide considerable evidence for exclusion of these four genes as candidates for the second locus on 19q13.3-->q13.4 in PJS.
we also excluded the recently identified STK11-interacting protein gene (STK11IP, alias LIP1) mapped in 2q36 as candidate for PJS in the PJS07 family

notes.statement: Keller et al. (2002) presented molecular genetic evidence of an association between nasal polyposis and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
quotes: Molecular genetic evidence of an association between nasal polyposis and the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

notes.statement: Olschwang et al. (2001) analyzed the STK11/LKB1 locus in 34 PJS families by mutation and rearrangement screening of the coding sequence, allele-specific expression tests, and linkage studies, and identified germline deleterious STK11 mutations in 70% of cases.
quotes: We report here the analysis of the STK11/LKB1 locus in a series of 34 PJS families, combining the search for mutations and rearrangements in the coding sequence, allele specific expression tests, and linkage studies.
Germline deleterious mutation of the STK11/LKB1 gene were identified in 70% of cases.

notes.statement: Olschwang et al. (2001) found that their data reinforced the hypothesis of a second PJS locus and concluded that up to 30% of PJS cases are caused by mutation in an unidentified gene conferring high susceptibility to cancer.
quotes: The hypothesis of a second PJS locus was reinforced
Up to 30% of PJS patients are caused by mutation in an unidentified gene that confers high susceptibility to cancer development.

notes.statement: Olschwang et al. (2001) found that cancer risk differed markedly between PJS families with and without an identified STK11 alteration; patients without an identified STK11 mutation were at major risk for proximal biliary adenocarcinoma, a tumor infrequent in the general population.
quotes: Analysis of clinical data indicates that the cancer associated risk is markedly different in the two groups.
PJS patients with no identified STK11/LKB1 mutation are at major risk for proximal biliary adenocarcinoma, an infrequent tumour in the general population.

notes.statement: Entius et al. (2001) found LOH at 19p13.3 (the STK11/LKB1 locus) in 15 of 39 hamartomatous polyps and in all 5 carcinomas from 17 PJS patients. Six of 7 polyps from patients with cancer showed LOH, compared with 9 of 31 polyps from the other patients (p = 0.01). The authors concluded that STK11 acts as a tumor suppressor and may be involved early in PJS tumorigenesis, and suggested that further research should test whether LOH in polyps could serve as a biomarker to predict cancer.
quotes: LOH at 19p was seen in 15 of the 39 polyps and in all carcinomas (n = 5). Interestingly, six of the seven polyps from patients with cancer had LOH, compared with nine of the 31 polyps from the remaining patients (p = 0.01).
These results provide further evidence that STK11/LKB1 acts as a tumour suppressor gene, and may be involved in the early stages of PJS tumorigenesis.

notes.statement: In PJS-related carcinomas, Entius et al. (2001) found no LOH at 5q, but APC mutations were present in 4 of 5 carcinomas. They found no 17p LOH and no p53 mutation. One carcinoma had an activating KRAS codon 12 mutation and another had 18q LOH without loss of SMAD4 expression. The authors suggested that the differences from the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence point to a distinct pathway of carcinogenesis.
quotes: No LOH at 5q was observed. However, mutational analysis revealed an APC mutation in four of the five carcinomas.
One carcinoma had an activating K-ras codon 12 mutation and another carcinoma showed 18q LOH; however, no loss of Smad4 expression was seen.
Differences in molecular genetic alterations noted between the adenoma-carcinoma sequence and PJS related tumours suggest the presence of a distinct pathway of carcinogenesis.

notes.statement: Entius et al. (2001) found no LOH at 19p, or at the alternative PJS candidate loci 19q, 6p, and 6q, in a polyp from a patient without a germline STK11 mutation.
quotes: In one polyp from a patient without a germline STK11/LKB1 mutation, no LOH at 19p or at three alternative PJS candidate loci (19q, 6p, and 6q) was found.

notes.statement: Miyaki et al. (2000) analyzed 27 gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps from 10 PJS patients in 9 families. They found somatic LKB1 mutations in 5 polyps and loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at the LKB1 locus on 19p in 14 other polyps. The polyps showed no APC mutation or 5q LOH, and K-ras mutations were detected in only a few polyps.
quotes: Somatic mutations of the LKB1 gene were found in 5 polyps, whereas loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at the LKB1 locus at 19p was seen in 14 other polyps.
K-ras mutations were detected in a few polyps, whereas no APC mutation or 5q LOH was detected in hamartomatous polyps.

notes.statement: Miyaki et al. (2000) found both a beta-catenin mutation and 19p LOH in adenomatous lesions microdissected from hamartomatous polyps. A carcinomatous lesion in a gastric polyp had a p53 mutation and p53 LOH in addition to LKB1 LOH and a beta-catenin mutation. The authors suggested that PJS polyps develop when the second LKB1 allele is inactivated by somatic mutation or LOH, and that further beta-catenin and p53 mutations convert hamartomas into adenomatous and carcinomatous lesions.
quotes: In adenomatous lesions microdissected from hamartomatous polyps, both beta-catenin mutation and 19p LOH were detected.
a carcinomatous lesion in a gastric hamartomatous polyp was found to contain a mutation of the p53 gene and LOH at the p53 locus in addition to LOH at the LKB1 locus and a beta-catenin mutation.

These results suggest that gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps in PJS patients develop through inactivation of the LKB1 gene by germ-line mutation plus somatic mutation or LOH of the unaffected LKB1 allele

notes.statement: Boardman et al. (2000) found LKB1 mutations in only 2 of 10 PJS probands with a family history and 4 of 23 sporadic PJS cases. They concluded that PJS shows significant genetic heterogeneity and that other loci are involved.
quotes: Mutation analysis revealed genetic alterations in LKB1 in two probands who had a family history of PJS.

LKB1 mutations were detected in only four of the remaining 23 cases of sporadic PJS. These data suggest the presence of significant genetic heterogeneity for PJS and the involvement of other loci in this syndrome.

notes.statement: Boardman et al. (2000) screened LKB1 with conformation sensitive gel electrophoresis followed by direct sequencing. They used long-range PCR to detect larger insertions or deletions.
quotes: Conformation sensitive gel electrophoresis was utilized for the initial screen, followed by direct sequence analysis for characterization. Long-range PCR was used for the detection of larger genetic insertions or deletions.

notes.statement: Bergadá et al. (2000) stated that gynecomastia in boys with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and Sertoli cell tumors of gonadal origin results from increased estrogen production due to increased aromatase activity within the testicular tumor. In their patient, the only abnormal hormonal finding was increased serum inhibin B and pro-alpha C.
quotes: Gynecomastia in boys with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and Sertoli cell tumors of gonadal origin results from increased estrogen production due to increased aromatase activity within the testicular tumor.

notes.statement: Jiang et al. (1999) screened 10 unrelated Peutz-Jeghers syndrome families for germline STK11 alterations using the protein truncation test and genomic sequencing. They found a novel truncating deletion of exons 2 through 7 in only one patient, and concluded that STK11 mutations account for only a proportion of PJS cases.
quotes: We conducted a detailed investigation of germline STK11 alterations by protein truncation test and genomic DNA sequence analysis in ten unrelated PJS families.
Our results suggest that STK11 mutations account for only a proportion of PJS cases.

notes.statement: Jiang et al. (1999) performed loss of heterozygosity studies in PJS polyps from 4 patients and identified an allelic deletion of the marker D19S886 in a patient other than the one carrying the germline STK11 deletion.
quotes: Loss of heterozygosity studies in PJS polyps of four of these patients identified an allelic deletion of D19S886 in another patient.

notes.statement: Westerman and Wilson (1999) reviewed the literature and noted that the polyps in PJS carry risks of surgical emergencies such as small bowel intussusception and of chronic or acute bleeding, and that PJS is associated with both gastrointestinal and non-gastrointestinal tumors, including rare tumors such as ovarian sex cord tumors with annular tubules, adenoma malignum of the cervix, and Sertoli cell tumors of the testis, indicating a general susceptibility to malignancy.
quotes: Risks imposed by the presence of polyps in PJS patients include surgical emergencies like small bowel intussusception, and chronic or acute bleeding from the polyps.

the frequent occurrence of some rare extra-intestinal malignancies such as tumours of the ovary (sex cord tumours with annular tubules), cervix (adenoma malignum) and testis (Sertoli cell tumours) indicates a general susceptibility for the development of malignancies.

notes.statement: Westerman and Wilson (1999) concluded that because genetic identification of asymptomatic gene carriers was becoming possible, surveillance and screening protocols needed to be developed for PJS patients and their relatives.
quotes: As genetic identification of asymptomatic gene carriers in this relatively rare disorder becomes possible, surveillance and screening protocols need to be developed for PJS patients and their relatives.

notes.statement: Westerman et al. (1999) performed mutation analysis in 19, predominantly Dutch, PJS families and identified 12 novel LKB1/STK11 mutations in 12 families (1 nonsense, 3 frameshift deletions, 3 frameshift insertions, 2 acceptor splice site, and 3 missense mutations). No mutation occurred in more than 1 family, and a number arose de novo; 4 polymorphisms were also detected.
quotes: We performed mutation analysis in 19, predominantly Dutch, PJS families. In 12 of these families, we identified LKB1/STK11 mutations, none of which has been described before.
In addition, we detected four polymorphisms in LKB1/STK11.
None of the mutations occurred in more than one family, and a number were demonstrated to have arisen de novo.

notes.statement: Westerman et al. (1999) found no apparent LKB1/STK11 abnormalities in 7 of 19 PJS families, which they suggested could reflect locus heterogeneity in PJS.
quotes: In the remaining seven PJS families, we found no apparent abnormalities of the LKB1/STK1I gene, which could reflect the existence of locus heterogeneity in PJS.

notes.statement: Westerman et al. (1999) concluded that the diverse array of mutations, the apparent high mutation rate, and a possible second PJS locus make diagnostic or predictive genetic testing in individual patients difficult.
quotes: The diverse array of mutations found, the apparent high mutation rate, as well as the existence of a possible second PJS locus, renders diagnostic or predictive genetic testing in individual patients difficult

notes.statement: Westerman et al. (1999) followed up the original Dutch family described by Peutz in 1921 for more than 78 years, across six generations. They concluded from the morbidity and mortality in the family that PJS is not a benign disease.
quotes: This original family has now been followed-up for more than 78 years.
The morbidity and mortality in this family suggest that PJS is not a benign disease.

notes.statement: Gruber et al. (1998) confirmed linkage of PJS to 19p13.3 near STK11 in the family originally described by Jeghers in 1949 and in 5 other families.
quotes: Linkage analysis in the family originally described by Jeghers in 1949 and five other families confirmed linkage to 19p13.3 near a recently identified gene responsible for PJS.

notes.statement: Gruber et al. (1998) found LOH of 19p markers near STK11 in 70% of hamartomas and adenocarcinomas from PJS patients. Haplotype analysis showed that the retained allele carried the germline mutation, which confirmed that STK11 is a tumor suppressor gene. The authors proposed that STK11 acts as an early gatekeeper regulating hamartoma development.
quotes: Analysis of hamartomas and adenocarcinomas from patients with PJS identified loss of heterozygosity (LOH) of 19p markers near STK11 in 70% of tumors.
Haplotype analysis indicated that the retained allele carried a germ-line mutation, confirming that STK11 is a tumor suppressor gene.
STK11 is a tumor suppressor gene that acts as an early gatekeeper regulating the development of hamartomas in PJS

notes.statement: Gruber et al. (1998) found LOH of 17p and 18q in an adenocarcinoma but not in hamartomas, implying that these are late events in PJS cancer pathogenesis. Adenocarcinomas with 17p LOH showed altered p53 by immunohistochemistry. None of 18 PJS tumors showed microsatellite instability, LOH at 5q near APC, or mutations in K-ras codons 12 or 13. The authors suggested that hamartomas may be precursors of adenocarcinoma.
quotes: LOH of 17p and 18q was identified in an adenocarcinoma but not in hamartomas, implying that allelic loss of these two regions corresponds to late molecular events in the pathogenesis of cancer in PJS.
None of the 18 PJS tumors showed microsatellite instability, LOH on 5q near APC, or mutations in codons 12 or 13 of the K-ras proto-oncogene.
suggest that hamartomas may be pathogenetic precursors of adenocarcinoma

notes.statement: Mehenni et al. (1998) screened 9 PJS families of American, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Turkish, and Indian origin for LKB1 mutations and found 7 novel mutations. These were 2 frameshift mutations, a 4-amino acid deletion, 2 amino acid substitutions, and 2 splicing errors.
quotes: we screened for LKB1 mutations in nine PJS families of American, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Turkish, and Indian origin and detected seven novel mutations. These included two frameshift mutations, one four-amino-acid deletion, two amino-acid substitutions, and two splicing errors.

notes.statement: Mehenni et al. (1998) expressed the mutant LKB1 proteins K78I, D176N, W308C, and L67P and found that all of them had lost autophosphorylation (kinase) activity. They concluded that loss of LKB1 kinase activity is probably responsible for the PJS phenotypes.
quotes: Expression of mutant LKB1 proteins (K78I, D176N, W308C, and L67P) and assessment of their autophosphorylation activity revealed a loss of the kinase activity in all of these mutants.
These results provide direct evidence that the elimination of the kinase activity of LKB1 is probably responsible for the development of the PJS phenotypes.

notes.statement: Mehenni et al. (1998) found no LKB1 mutation in 2 Indian PJS families. They had previously detected linkage to markers on 19q13.3-q13.4 in one of these families, which suggested locus heterogeneity of PJS.
quotes: In two Indian families, we failed to detect any LKB1 mutation; in one of these families, we previously had detected linkage to markers on 19q13.3-4, which suggests locus heterogeneity of PJS.

notes.statement: Kato et al. (1998) treated labial lentigines in 2 children with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome with ruby laser therapy; the response was excellent, with no sequelae or recurrence. They suggested that ruby laser therapy is safe and suitable for labial lentigines in children with PJS.
quotes: The response to treatment was excellent and no sequelae or recurrence of the lesions was noted.
Our experience suggests that ruby laser therapy is safe and a suitable approach for the treatment of labial lentigines in children with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

notes.statement: Olschwang et al. (1998) analyzed 20 more Peutz-Jeghers syndrome families. Most were consistent with a PJS gene on 19p13.3, which supports a major PJS locus on that chromosome.
quotes: We have analysed 20 further families and found that the majority of these are consistent with a PJS gene on 19p13.3.
There appears, therefore, to be a major PJS locus on chromosome 19p13.3

notes.statement: Olschwang et al. (1998) found 3 of 20 PJS families unlinked to 19p13.3. None of the available polyps from these families showed allele loss at D19S886. There were no obvious clinicopathologic or ethnic differences between linked and unlinked families. The authors suggested there may be a minor locus (or loci) elsewhere.
quotes: Three families were, however, unlinked to 19p13.3 and none of the available PJS polyps from these families showed allele loss at D19S886.
There were no obvious clinicopathological or ethnic differences between the 19p13.3 linked and unlinked families.
the possibility exists of a minor locus (or loci) elsewhere

notes.statement: Hemminki et al. (1998) identified truncating germline mutations in LKB1, a gene on chromosome 19p, in multiple individuals with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. They concluded that PJS was the first cancer-susceptibility syndrome found to be caused by inactivating mutations in a protein kinase.
quotes: We have identified truncating germline mutations in a gene residing on chromosome 19p in multiple individuals affected by PJS.
Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is therefore the first cancer-susceptibility syndrome to be identified that is due to inactivating mutations in a protein kinase.

notes.statement: Hemminki et al. (1998) noted that LKB1, a gene that had been identified before but not mapped, was strongly homologous to XEEK1, a cytoplasmic serine/threonine protein kinase in Xenopus. It was also more weakly similar to many other protein kinases.
quotes: This previously identified but unmapped gene, LKB1, has strong homology to a cytoplasmic Xenopus serine/threonine protein kinase XEEK1, and weaker similarity to many other protein kinases.

notes.statement: Hemminki et al. (1998) described Peutz-Jeghers syndrome as a rare hereditary disease that predisposes to benign and malignant tumors in many organ systems.
quotes: the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS), a rare hereditary disease in which there is predisposition to benign and malignant tumours of many organ systems.

notes.statement: Jenne et al. (1998) identified a novel serine threonine kinase gene, STK11, located 190 kb proximal to marker D19S886 in the 19p13.3 Peutz-Jeghers linkage region. They found five germline STK11 mutations, all predicted to disrupt the kinase domain. They concluded that germline STK11 mutations, probably together with acquired defects of the second allele in somatic cells, cause Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
quotes: In a distance of 190 kb proximal to D19S886, we identified and characterized a novel human gene encoding the serine threonine kinase STK11.
All five germline mutations are predicted to disrupt the function of the kinase domain.
We conclude that germline mutations in STK11, probably in conjunction with acquired genetic defects of the second allele in somatic cells, cause the manifestations of PJ syndrome.

notes.statement: Jenne et al. (1998) described Peutz-Jeghers syndrome as an autosomal dominant disorder with melanocytic macules of the lips, multiple gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps, and a higher risk of various neoplasms, including gastrointestinal cancer.
quotes: Peutz-Jeghers (PJ) syndrome is an autosomal-dominant disorder characterized by melanocytic macules of the lips, multiple gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps and an increased risk for various neoplasms, including gastrointestinal cancer.

notes.statement: Mehenni et al. (1997) did a genomewide linkage analysis in 6 PJS families with 39 affected members and confirmed linkage to 19p13.3. Marker D19S886 gave a maximum lod score of 4.74 at theta = 0.045, and multipoint analysis gave a lod score of 7.51 for the interval between D19S886 and 19pter.
quotes: For our families, marker D19S886 yielded a maximum LOD score of 4.74 at a recombination fraction (theta) of .045; multipoint linkage analysis resulted in a LOD score of 7.51 for the interval between D19S886 and 19 pter.

notes.statement: Mehenni et al. (1997) also found significant evidence for linkage to markers on 19q13.4; for example, D19S880 gave a maximum lod score of 3.8 at theta = 0.13. Most of this signal came from a single family, PJS07. The authors suggested that a potential second PJS locus on 19q13.4 may exist in a minority of families.
quotes: However, markers on 19q13.4 also showed significant evidence for linkage. For example, D19S880 resulted in a maximum LOD score of 3.8 at theta = .13. Most of this positive linkage was contributed by a single family, PJS07.
but also suggest the existence, in a minority of families, of a potential second PJS locus, on 19q13.4

notes.statement: Mehenni et al. (1997) described PJS as an autosomal dominant disease with variable expression and incomplete penetrance.
quotes: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS) is an autosomal dominant disease with variable expression and incomplete penetrance, characterized by mucocutaneous pigmentation and hamartomatous polyposis.

notes.statement: Mehenni et al. (1997) noted that PJS is characterized by mucocutaneous pigmentation and hamartomatous polyposis. They also noted that patients have an increased frequency of gastrointestinal and extraintestinal malignancies, including those of the ovaries, testes, and breast.
quotes: characterized by mucocutaneous pigmentation and hamartomatous polyposis. Patients with PJS have increased frequency of gastrointestinal and extraintestinal malignancies (ovaries, testes, and breast).

notes.statement: Amos et al. (1997) confirmed that PJS maps to the telomeric region of chromosome 19p and narrowed the locus further. In 5 families there were no recombinants with marker D19S886, and the multipoint lod score at D19S886 was 7.52.
quotes: Our studies confirm this location and provide further localization of the PJS locus.
In the five families examined, there were no recombinants with the marker D19S886. The multipoint log odds score at D19S886 is 7.52

notes.statement: Amos et al. (1997) found no evidence of genetic heterogeneity among the 5 PJS families they studied.
quotes: we found no evidence for genetic heterogeneity

notes.statement: Amos et al. (1997) found that every carrier of the linked haplotype expressed the PJS phenotype and that no noncarrier showed PJS features. They took this to indicate complete penetrance with no sporadic cases.
quotes: We also found that all carriers expressed the PJS phenotype and no noncarriers displayed PJS sequellae, indicating complete penetrance with no sporadic cases.

notes.statement: Hemminki et al. (1997) used comparative genomic hybridization (CGH) of Peutz-Jeghers polyps combined with loss of heterozygosity (LOH) analysis to identify a deletion site, and then performed linkage analysis with markers from this region in 12 families. They found a high-penetrance locus in distal 19p, with a multipoint lod score of 7.00 at marker D19S886.
quotes: A search for a putative tumour suppressor locus was made using comparative genomic hybridization (CGH) of Peutz-Jeghers polyps, combined with loss of heterozygosity (LOH) study.
Genetic linkage analysis in 12 families using markers from a deletion site demonstrated the presence of a high-penetrance locus in distal 19p with a multipoint lod score of 7.00 at marker D19S886

notes.statement: Hemminki et al. (1997) found no evidence of genetic heterogeneity among 12 Peutz-Jeghers families linked to distal 19p.
quotes: multipoint lod score of 7.00 at marker D19S886 without evidence of genetic heterogeneity

notes.statement: Hemminki et al. (1997) suggested that the deletions/LOH at 19p in Peutz-Jeghers polyps pointed to a tumor suppressor locus and provided molecular evidence of malignant potential in hamartomas.
quotes: The study demonstrates the power of CGH combined with LOH analysis in identifying putative tumour suppressor loci, and provides molecular evidence of malignant potential in hamartomas.

notes.statement: Hemminki et al. (1997) described Peutz-Jeghers syndrome as a condition characterized by intestinal hamartomatous polyposis and melanin spots of the lips, buccal mucosa and digits, with a dramatically elevated risk of malignancy, including gastrointestinal tumors and cancers of the breast, ovary, testis, and uterine cervix.
quotes: a condition characterized by intestinal hamartomatous polyposis and melanin spots of the lips, buccal mucosa and digits. A dramatically elevated risk of malignancy has also been documented.
Gastrointestinal tumours as well as cancers of the breast, ovary, testis and uterine cervix appear to be overrepresented in families with this syndrome.

notes.statement: Markie et al. (1996) found a pericentric inversion of chromosome 6 in a patient with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. FISH with YAC clones placed one breakpoint within the centromeric alphoid array, in a 1-cM interval between D6S257 and D6S402. It placed the other breakpoint in a 4-cM interval between D6S403 and D6S311.
quotes: Karyotypic analysis in a patient with Peutz-Jeghers' syndrome demonstrated a pericentric inversion on chromosome 6.
This analysis located one inversion breakpoint within the alphoid array, in a 1-cM interval between D6S257 and D6S402, and the other in a 4-cM interval between D6S403 and D6S311.

notes.statement: Markie et al. (1996) excluded the estrogen receptor gene locus (ESR) from the 4-cM interval that contained the distal inversion breakpoint in their patient with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
quotes: The oestrogen receptor gene locus (ESR) is excluded from the latter interval.

notes.statement: Young et al. (1995) found increased transcription of the aromatase cytochrome P450 gene from promoter II, the promoter used in normal ovary and testis, in testicular tumor tissue from 2 boys with PJS. Transcript levels were comparable to corpus luteum and led to increased estrogen synthesis. Transcripts from the placental-type promoters I.1 and I.2 were not found at significant levels.
quotes: Studies of testicular tumor tissue from both cases revealed increased transcription of the aromatase cytochrome P450 gene using promoter II, the promoter directing aromatase expression in the normal ovary and testis.
The levels of transcripts were comparable to corpus luteum, thus resulting in increased estrogen synthesis.
Transcripts specific for placental-type aromatase promoters (I.1 and I.2) were not detected in significant levels in these tumors.

notes.statement: Young et al. (1995) performed bilateral orchiectomy in 2 boys with PJS and feminizing Sertoli cell tumors. The reasons were that the tumor growth would most likely cause sterility, and that continued high estradiol levels threatened to reduce height potential.
quotes: Bilateral orchiectomy was performed in each case because the neoplastic growth would most likely result in sterility, and curtailment of height potential was threatened from continued elevation of estradiol levels.

notes.statement: Young et al. (1995) described the tumor pathology. Microscopy showed greatly enlarged seminiferous tubules packed with Sertoli-like cells, and prominent eosinophilic basement membrane that formed hyalinized globules and microcalcifications. Electron microscopy showed laminated basement membranes and limited smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
quotes: Microscopically, greatly enlarged seminiferous tubules packed with ovoid Sertoli-like cells were present. Prominent eosinophilic basement membrane surrounded the tubules and intersected between the cells, forming hyalinized ovoid globules and microcalcifications.
Ultrastructure revealed lamination of basement membranes surrounding adjacent cells, ovoid cells with abundant cytoplasm, and limited smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

notes.statement: Péloquin et al. (1981) reviewed the literature on metastatic Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and concluded that, although the rate of metastatic disease is low, all patients with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome deserve close long-term follow-up.
quotes: Although the rate of metastatic disease is low, they believe that all patients with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome deserve a close long-term follow-up.

notes.statement: Griffith and Bisset (1980) reported 3 cases of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome presenting in early childhood and considered the need for surgical intervention.
quotes: We report 3 cases of the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome presenting in early childhood, and consider the need for surgical intervention.

notes.statement: Riley and Swift (1980) noted that breast cancer had been reported before in patients with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. They suggested that the Peutz-Jeghers gene may be associated with an increased risk of breast tumors.
quotes: Because there are previous reports of breast cancer in patients with this syndrome, the Peutz-Jeghers gene may be associated with an increased risk of breast tumors.

notes.statement: Burdick and Prior (1982) documented at postmortem an adenocarcinoma of the jejunum arising in a Peutz-Jeghers polyp, with metastases in the mesenteric lymph nodes. They concluded that the exact risk of intestinal cancer in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome was unknown but probably very small.
quotes: Postmortem examination revealed this to be an adenocarcinoma of the jejunum arising in a Peutz-Jeghers polyp and metastases were present in the mesenteric lymph nodes.
the exact risk of intestinal cancer in the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is unknown, but probably very small

notes.statement: Burdick and Prior (1982) recommended continuing gastrointestinal surgery in symptomatic patients and close follow-up of all patients at regular intervals.
quotes: Gastrointestinal surgery should continue to be performed in symptomatic patients and all patients should be followed closely at regular intervals.

notes.statement: Yamada et al. (1981) reported ultrastructural studies of the pigmented macules of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
quotes: Ultrastructural studies on pigmented macules of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

notes.statement: DiLiberti et al. (1983) described a 7.5-year-old boy who had macrocephaly, hamartomatous intestinal polyps, and cafe-au-lait spots on the penis. They proposed that this triad was a separate disorder, the Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome, which is distinct from other hamartomatous polyposis conditions. His mother's macrocephaly, similar facial appearance, and hamartomatous polyp suggested dominant inheritance.
quotes: We report on a 7 1/2-year-old boy with macrocephaly, hamartomatous intestinal polyps, and café-au-lait spots on the penis.
We think that this triad of abnormalities represents a new disorder, the Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome.
Macrocephaly, similar facial appearance, and a hamartomatous polyp in the mother suggest dominant inheritance.

notes.statement: Cantú et al. (1980) found that the raised estrogen levels in their patient's Sertoli cell tumor did not change with exogenous gonadotropin administration, which indicated autonomous production. Histology of the nontumorous testicular tissue suggested that estrogens may have had both stimulating and atrophying effects on the seminiferous tubules.
quotes: The increased levels of estrogens did not show changes that could be correlated with exogenous gonadotropin administration, thus indicating an autonomous nature.

The histopathologic studies of nontumorous testicular tissue revealed changes in the seminiferous tubules which suggested that estrogens, directly or indirectly, may have had both stimulating and atrophying effects.

notes.statement: Cantú et al. (1980) concluded that gonadal tumors are an additional manifestation of the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome gene in both male and female patients.
quotes: It is concluded that gonadal tumors are in additional manifestation of the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome gene in both male and female patients.

notes.statement: Solh et al. (1983) reported Peutz-Jeghers syndrome associated with precocious puberty.
quotes: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome associated with precocious puberty.

notes.statement: Tweedie and McCann (1984) noted that serum CEA was normal at presentation in their patient with PJS and metastasizing colonic adenocarcinoma, as in one other reported case, and concluded that CEA determination as a screening test in high-risk groups was not supported.
quotes: The serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) was normal at presentation in this patient and in one other reported case.
The use of this determination as a screening test for so-called high risk groups is, therefore, not supported by this report.

notes.statement: Tweedie and McCann (1984) could not determine whether the colonic carcinoma in their PJS patient had arisen from a Peutz-Jeghers polyp, and stated that the risk of malignancy in PJS was unknown and would require follow-up of a defined PJS population compared with a matched general population sample.
quotes: It was not possible to determine whether the carcinoma had arisen from a Peutz-Jeghers polyp.

The risk of malignancy is not known. It will only be determined by careful follow up of a defined Peutz-Jeghers syndrome population and comparison of carcinoma incidence with a matched sample of the general population.

notes.statement: Sommerhaug and Mason (1970) reported Peutz-Jeghers syndrome together with ureteral polyposis.
quotes: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and ureteral polyposis.

notes.statement: Scully (1970) described sex cord tumor with annular tubules as a distinctive ovarian tumor of the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
quotes: Sex cord tumor with annular tubules a distinctive ovarian tumor of the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

notes.statement: Dodds et al. (1972) discussed gastrointestinal malignancy in association with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
quotes: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and gastrointestinal malignancy.

notes.statement: Bowlby (1986) reported a 16-year-old male with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and pancreatic adenocarcinoma, which the author believed to be the first reported association of PJS with carcinoma of the pancreas.
quotes: The present case of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome in a 16-year-old male is the first, to the author's knowledge, to be reported in association with carcinoma of the pancreas.

notes.statement: Wilson et al. (1986) concluded from their case and other reports in the literature that males with PJS, as well as females, are at risk for developing gonadal tumors.
quotes: This case and other reports from the literature suggest that males, as well as females, with PJS are at risk for developing gonadal tumors.

notes.statement: Giardiello et al. (1987) found that cancers in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome patients were diagnosed at a relatively young age but after the diagnosis of PJS (interval 25 +/- 20 years; range 1 to 64), and that the observed development of cancer was 18 times greater than expected in the general population (P less than 0.0001), suggesting increased risk at gastrointestinal and nongastrointestinal sites.
quotes: The cancers were diagnosed when the patients were relatively young, but after the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome had been diagnosed (interval between diagnoses, 25 +/- 20 years; range, 1 to 64).
the observed development of cancer in the patients with the syndrome was 18 times greater than expected in the general population (P less than 0.0001)

notes.statement: Giardiello et al. (1987) described Peutz-Jeghers syndrome as an autosomal dominant hereditary disease characterized by hamartomatous polyps of the gastrointestinal tract and mucocutaneous melanin deposits.
quotes: The Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is an autosomal dominant hereditary disease characterized by hamartomatous polyps of the gastrointestinal tract and by mucocutaneous melanin deposits.

notes.statement: Foley et al. (1988) recommended that even asymptomatic gastric, duodenal, and colonic polyps be removed endoscopically in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, that intraoperative endoscopy with polypectomy be used when surgery is necessary to prevent short bowel syndrome, and that colonoscopic screening and surveillance for extraintestinal malignancy appeared warranted.
quotes: Consequently, even asymptomatic gastric, duodenal, and colonic polyps should be removed endoscopically. If surgical intervention is necessary, intraoperative endoscopy with polypectomy may prevent the development of a short bowel syndrome.
Colonoscopic screening of patients and their family members may be beneficial and surveillance for extraintestinal malignancy appears to be warranted.

notes.statement: Foley et al. (1988) concluded from 49-year follow-up of the Harrisburg family that Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is not a benign disease and may be a premalignant condition.
quotes: The course of this family illustrates that Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is not a benign disease.
The development of gastrointestinal malignancy in 2 of 12 affected patients suggests that Peutz-Jeghers syndrome may be a premalignant condition.

notes.statement: Spigelman et al. (1989) found that among 72 patients with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, 16 (22%) developed malignant tumors (9 gastrointestinal, 7 nongastrointestinal), and all but 1 of these died. The relative risks of death from gastrointestinal cancer and from all cancers were 13 and 9, respectively, and the chance of dying of cancer by age 57 years was 48%.
quotes: Among 72 patients with the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome malignant tumours have developed in 16 (22%) of whom all but one have died.
The relative risks of death from gastrointestinal cancer and all cancers were 13 (95% CI 2.7-38.1) and 9 (95% CI 4.2-17.3) respectively.
The chance of dying of cancer by the age of 57 was 48%.

notes.statement: Spigelman et al. (1989) concluded that there was evidence for a hamartoma/carcinoma sequence in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, suggesting that the gene locus involved is relevant to the development of malignancy in general.
quotes: There is evidence for a hamartoma/carcinoma sequence in the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, suggesting that the gene locus involved is relevant to the development of malignancy in general.

notes.statement: Eng et al. (1991) reported a 67-year-old white man with esophageal adenocarcinoma who had Peutz-Jeghers-like macules on the lips, face, nipples and rectal mucosa. Pathological examination of the macules showed atypical, pleomorphic large melanocytes in the epidermis that resembled the neoplastic cells of melanoma in situ. The authors stated that this was the first report of atypical melanocyte proliferation in Peutz-Jeghers-like melanosis associated with a primary esophageal adenocarcinoma.
quotes: A 67-year-old white man with esophageal adenocarcinoma presented with Peutz-Jeghers-like macules on the lips, face, nipples, and rectal mucosa.
The pleomorphic large melanocytes resembled the neoplastic cells seen in melanoma in situ.
This is the first report of proliferation of atypical melanocytes in Peutz-Jeghers-like melanosis associated with a primary esophageal adenocarcinoma.

notes.statement: Veraldi et al. (1991) described 4 adults (2 men and 2 women aged 39 to 57 years) with Laugier-Hunziker syndrome. All had pigmentation of the lower lip and hard palate, and some also had pigmentation of the buccal mucosa, upper lip, gums, soft palate and fingers. Histopathology showed melanin accumulated in basal layer keratinocytes and more melanophages in the papillary dermis. Melanocytes were not altered.
quotes: In all patients (two men and two women between 39 and 57 years of age) pigmentation of the lower lip and hard palate was found.
Histopathologic examination demonstrated an accumulation of melanin in the basal layer keratinocytes and an increase in the number of melanophages in the papillary dermis.
Alterations of the melanocytes were not observed.

notes.statement: Gass and Glatzer (1991) described a 74-year-old man with an occult carcinoma of the colon. He developed acquired pigmentation of the mouth and penis typical of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome as the first sign of bilateral diffuse uveal melanocytic proliferation. The authors suggested that the pigmented lesions may come from activation of occult melanocytic naevus cells in response to a hormone-producing carcinoma or another oncogenic stimulus.
quotes: A 74-year-old man with an occult carcinoma of the colon developed pigmentation of the mouth and penis typical of the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome as the first manifestation of bilateral diffuse uveal melanocytic proliferation.

bilateral diffuse uveal melanocytic proliferation may be caused by activation of occult melanocytic naevus cells in response to either a hormone-producing carcinoma or to some other common oncogenic stimulus

notes.statement: Kallioniemi et al. (1992) described comparative genomic hybridization, which maps DNA sequence copy number by chromosomal location across the whole genome. Differentially labeled test DNA and normal reference DNA are hybridized together to normal chromosome spreads. Gains and losses show up as changes in the ratio of the two fluorochrome intensities.
quotes: Comparative genomic hybridization produces a map of DNA sequence copy number as a function of chromosomal location throughout the entire genome.

Regions of gain or loss of DNA sequences, such as deletions, duplications, or amplifications, are seen as changes in the ratio of the intensities of the two fluorochromes along the target chromosomes.

notes.statement: Lin et al. (1977) noted that of 14 reported cases of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome associated with intestinal carcinoma, in only 2 was the tumor shown to originate in the polyp; in their own patient they believed the duodenal carcinoma developed independently. They stated that duodenal carcinoma is the most commonly associated neoplasm.
quotes: Of 14 reported cases of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome associated with intestinal carcinoma, in only two was the tumor shown to originate in the polyp. In our case, too, we believe the carcinoma developed independently.
Duodenal carcinoma is the most commonly associated neoplasm.

notes.statement: Babin et al. (1978) reported a case in which melanocytes of the oral and laryngeal mucosa caused hyperpigmentation in response to an occult malignancy. They discussed how to distinguish this from other disease processes that cause oral hyperpigmentation.
quotes: Melanocytes exist in the oral and laryngeal mucosa capable of responding with a hyperpigmentation response to occult malignancy. Such a case is presented and its differentiation from other disease processes is discussed.

notes.statement: McAllister and Richards (1977) reported 20 patients with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome across five generations of one family. They discussed how the spots and polyps develop and relate to each other, and described a previously unreported case of colon intussusception.
quotes: One of us (AJM) has the largest personal series in the literature with twenty patients in five generations.
Pedigree charts and aspects relating to the development and interrelationships of spots and polyps are explained.

notes.statement: Matuchansky et al. (1979) provided histologic evidence that malignancy can arise in a Peutz-Jeghers hamartomatous polyp: in their patient, the adenocarcinoma was closely intermingled with smooth muscle bands, and a well-defined transitional zone of malignant cells was seen in several glands of the degenerated polyp. Glands near the malignant areas had less-differentiated epithelium but were still mixed with nonstriated muscle bundles, which the authors considered strong evidence that the hamartomatous structures had dedifferentiated.
quotes: Adenocarcinoma was intimately intricated with smooth muscle bands, and well-defined transitional zone of malignant cells could be observed in several glands of the degenerated P-J polyp

close to malignant areas, glands of this polyp exhibited a less-differentiated epithelium, but were still intermixed with nonstriated muscle bundles, which strongly suggest dedifferentiation of hamartomatous structures.

notes.statement: Joishy et al. (1979) reported a patient with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome whose successive intussusceptions required extensive small bowel resection. They reviewed the literature on diagnosing and managing complications of the syndrome.
quotes: Our experience is compared with that of other authors by a review of the literature highlighting important points in the diagnosis and management of complications in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

notes.statement: Cochet et al. (1979) found dysplastic areas within the hamartomatous polyps of a mother and son with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, both of whom had metastasising carcinoma. The authors concluded that hamartomatous polyps may, in some cases, be precursors of digestive tract carcinomas.
quotes: Both cases also showed dysplastic areas within hamartomatous polyps. These features indicate that hamartomatous polyps may, in some cases, be the precursors of digestive tract carcinomas.
